entityDescription: The Seatizens for Plankton Planet (S4P2) Association is a non-profit non-governmental organization governed by French law, specifically the 1901 law on associations. Founded in 2016 during the pilot phase of the Plankton Planet project (Vargas et al., 2022, Frontiers in Marine Science), S4P2 brings together “seatizens”— i.e. all sorts of seafarers and sea users - who are eager to discover, measure, and understand the invisible living majority in the oceans: plankton or the ocean microbiome. The Association has two primary missions: (i) ocean microbiome literacy to raise awareness about planktonic ecosystems, and (ii) the recruitment, training, and coordination of seatizens to build up a cooperative, cost-effective, and sustainable global measurement of aquatic microscopic life. Overall, the goal of the Plankton Planet initiative (in which S4P2 is one of the running entity) is to establish, by 2030, the first seatizen-based standard measure of the surface ocean microbiome across planetary scales, allowing to monitor and understand the evolution and health of the ocean.

entityDescription:
The Professorship for Space Technology focuses its research on three main areas: Nanosatellites for Extraterrestrial Missions, Space Systems & Higher Autonomy, and UAP & SETI Research.

Key achievements include the fully in-house developed, built, and operated nanosatellite missions SONATE and SONATE-2. SONATE-2, a 6U+ satellite launched in 2024, integrates AI technologies for in-orbit training and features an electric propulsion system and a novell star tracker, building on the experiences and components of its predecessor. The earlier SONATE mission pioneered autonomy in nanosatellites with systems like ASAP-Light for automated event detection and ADIA-Light for onboard diagnostics.

The professorship also operates a remote-controlled telescope in Spain for the detection of lunar transient phenomena, a telescope in Würzburg for SSA research, and a SkyCam-System for UAP detection. Additional expertise includes the design, construction, and operation of star trackers and subsystems for small satellites, as well as research into autorotative landing systems for interplanetary missions.

The Baltic Marine Environment Protection Commission – also known as the “Helsinki Commission” or “HELCOM” – was established in 1974 pursuant to and at the same time as theConvention on the Protection of the Marine Environment of the Baltic Sea Area(the “Helsinki Convention”).
The Helsinki Commission meets annually, with allContracting Partiesparticipating: Denmark, Estonia, the European Union, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Russia and Sweden. In addition, meetings at the Ministerial level are held every few years (usually every three years). The Contracting Parties are represented by Heads of Delegation (HOD).
The Commission adoptsRecommendationsrelated to the protection of the marine environment and sustainable maritime activities, decides on the budget and makes other key decisions. Decisions are made by consensus.
Thechairmanshipof the Commission rotates between the Contracting Parties every two years, according to their alphabetical order in English, the working language of the Commission.
The working structure of HELCOM consists of the meetings of the Helsinki Commission, the Heads of Delegation, and the eight mainHELCOM Working Groups. The HELCOM work and meetings are coordinated by the HELCOM Secretariat.

The HELCOM Secretariat coordinates the work and meetings of the Helsinki Commission, and ensures that theContracting Partiesmeet their obligations under theHelsinki Convention. The headquarters of HELCOM, the Secretariat, is located in Helsinki, Finland.

Our story began in 2020, when, after decades of working on the development of the first humanoid robots commercialized worldwide, we founded Keybotic in Barcelona with the goal of developing robotic technology to meet the specific needs of the industrial sector. We encountered dangerous inspections carried out by people because there were no alternatives: a maintenance technician supervising the plant and visually checking the equipment, inspecting confined spaces, or manually reading gauges in areas with toxic or asphyxiating gases.
To address this issue, Keybotic built fully autonomous robot dogs capable of accessing any location a human could reach, including stairs and unstable terrain, for industrial inspections. With this technology, we won first place at the DARPA Robotics Challenge, competing against MIT and the world’s best universities. This victory earned us the highest global recognition in robotics, awarded by the United States government, confirming that our autonomy and fleet coordination capabilities are the most advanced in the world.
The Keyper can access any area, including those dangerous for humans, and autonomously monitor facilities. It detects gas leaks, hot spots, steam leaks, reads instruments, detects intruders, and sends real-time alarms to the control center. Additionally, it generates 3D maps with point clouds to be used by engineering departments. In other words, the Keyper performs fully autonomous maintenance and security routes, inspecting facilities and alerting when there is an issue. This improves personnel safety, increases production uptime, and reduces costs through continuous monitoring and predictive maintenance.

It should be noted that Frederick University is the registered Trade/Business name of Mesokeleas Ltd. I.e. both names correspond to the same legal entity. 
Frederick University (FredU) is an energetic and vibrant private university operating in the Republic of Cyprus. Since its establishment (2007), FredU managed to achieve significant growth, both in terms of student population, faculty members, and academic infrastructure. FredU employs about 250 (fte) faculty, with 4500 students enrolled annually on average and operates from two campuses. FredU is recognized as the University that offers novel and innovative programs of study that address societal needs and, primarily, as the university that exhibits high social sensitivity and responsibility. It offers a broad range of academic programs of study (more than 80) in the areas of Science, Engineering, Business, Arts, Architecture, Media, Humanities, Health, and Education. FredU has also developed the necessary experience and e-learning infrastructure for offering accredited programs of study through Distance Learning and has been awarded with the E-xcellence Associates in Quality label. 
Furthermore, FredU hosts an "UNESCO Chair on Lifelong Learning and Adult Education" since 2020. In the same year, FredU joined the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), becoming one of the founding members of Cyprus' national network. In the latest Times Higher Education Impact Rankings 2023, Frederick University ranked among the top 201-300 Universities, the only University in Cyprus and Greece to achieve this. It has also scored highly for its positive impact and meaningful work on specific SDGs, having ranked 44th globally for Quality Education (SDG4) and 100th for Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG7). As part of its internationalization strategy and further engagement with ERA and EEA, FredU has also joint EU CONEXUS a European University alliance for Smart Urban Coastal Sustainability. Furthermore, FredU has been ranked in the top 200 universities in the world in the QS International Trade Rankings 2023. Being the only Cypriot university to appear in this ranking indicates the strength and dominance of our Maritime Commence & Transport Department in the field.
FredU's academic staff, either organized in multidisciplinary teams or individually, is involved in a wide range of research, educational and cultural activities relevant to their specializations. The research initiatives and activities that are being carried out by its faculty, have been funded predominantly from external sources through competitive national and European programs, including HORIZON Europe/2020, LIFE, ERASMUS+, ESA, FP7 and from Regional Funds (INTERREG). Besides the self-funded creative and other projects, the University staff has implemented or currently running more than 320 RDI and consulting projects, the majority of which coordinated by FredU faculty and researchers. As a consequence, the necessary services have been developed (e.g. Research & Interconnection, Financial, International & Public Relations) that provide the required support for the administrative, legal and financial management of funded projects.

Eletoyia is a pioneering company in the development and installation of photovoltaic systems in Cyprus. It is heavily involved in all aspects of scientific research into renewable energy generation, consumption, storage and distribution using photovoltaic systems in collaboration with European and National projects. Eletoyia’s deep scientific understanding of photovoltaic systems on an academic level, and practical market understanding gained through substantial commercial installation operations in Cyprus, allow the company to have a unique perspective, and understanding of innovative, practical and disruptive solutions.
More specifically, Eletoyia is an SME which deals with the study, R&D, design, installation, development, maintenance, operation, assessment, analysis and management of small residential PV plants, isolated off-grid autonomous systems and microgrids, industrial plants and large commercial PV plants. Its vision is to make smart technologies in the Energy Sector accessible to industrial operators, to design methodologies as well as algorithms and solutions, by combining state-of-the-art research, crowdsourcing and machine learning.
